title: Summary Template Plan
eyebrow: Build plan · the summary page template and the define-before-use rule · house-rules 2.68.4 to 2.69.0

short.lead: This is the build plan for your four answers on the summary template proposal (docs/plans/2026-10-19-summary-template.html). Those answers were: the template lives in the plugin; each answer is named in words; your define-before-use rule joins the existing writing rule; and summary pages get short lines and a before-and-after strip. The work is 4 steps, each its own GitHub issue under one parent issue, built one at a time by a helper agent. Everything below starts from main, where the plugin is version 2.68.4. Question 1 at the bottom of this page, "Which branch does the work happen on?", needs your answer before I start.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it creates or changes and what it needs from you.
items: file
Step 1
The rule wording

In rules/clear-writing.md, the "Explicit context" and "Named references" lines merge into one line, "Define before use": name what a phrase means before its first use, so nothing is inferred, and when that genuinely can't be done, say plainly why. The detail file, rules/detail/clear-writing.md, gets examples, including a reference like "round 1, answer 7" rewritten as what that answer actually decided. verify.py lists the rule's line names at verify.py:358 and verify.py:1939, so both lists are updated in the same change.
Nothing from you. Done when verify.py passes with the new line names.
search
Step 2
The checker learns round, question and answer references

scripts/clarity.py, the writing checker that runs on replies, pages and new issues, already flags a bare issue number or option letter (clarity.py:135). It also starts flagging "question N" and "answer N", alone or after "round N", when the words that follow do not say what the question was or what the answer decided. This passes, because it says what was asked and answered: "Round 2, question 1, where the agent's name comes from: the GitHub login plus sAgent". This is flagged, because it says neither: "see round 1, answer 7". verify.py gets one passing and one flagged case for each.
Nothing from you. Done when the new verify.py cases pass and no existing case breaks.
swap
Step 3
The template, the page builder and the starter file

templates/handover-page.html gains three optional features, so every existing page builds unchanged. A page whose content file contains "kind": "summary" labels the second box in each row "Decided by" instead of "Requires". A row's "Creates or changes" text can be a list, drawn as one short line per decision. A row can carry the existing before-and-after strip ("What exists today → What this creates → How it impacts you", handover-page.html:367), which today only the changes section draws. scripts/make_page.py stops with an error if "kind" is anything other than "summary". A new starter file, templates/decision-summary.page.json, holds the shape, and rules/detail/show-dont-tell.md says every grilling, restructure or brainstorm summary starts from it.
Nothing from you. Done when verify.py builds a summary page in Chromium at phone width, light and dark, with no clipped text.
check
Step 4
Docs, version and QA page

docs/4-systems/handover-pages.md gets a section on summary pages. The plugin version goes from 2.68.4 to 2.69.0. The real test: the grilling summary page (docs/plans/2026-10-19-grilling-summary.html) is rebuilt from the starter file, with every "Decided by" box naming the round, the question and the answer in words. A QA page (the page you review at the end) lists what was built, how each part was checked, and what stays unverified.
You open the rebuilt grilling summary page, check it, and reply with "QA passed: summary template" or "QA failed: summary template".

It holds the shape you rated 9 out of 10 in your reply on the grilling summary: one row per topic, short lines of what each decision creates or changes, the before-and-after strip, and a "Decided by" box naming each answer in words.
